diagram_classification: cosmological / computistical (a wheel diagram of time or the heavens, probably a division of the year or day into twelve parts)
interpretation: The diagram is a wheel with a green outer rim, a small central hub ringed in reddish-pink, and twelve spokes. The spokes alternate in colour between green, pink and ochre, and each is joined to the rim and hub by small curved fillets. No labels or inscriptions belong to the diagram itself. The text visible behind it is bleed-through from the other side of the leaf and is not part of the figure. The twelve equal divisions suggest a cyclical scheme of time, such as the twelve months, twelve hours or twelve signs, or possibly the twelve winds. The empty hub and rim mean that nothing can be assigned to individual spokes. Any more specific meaning, and the role of the colour alternation, is uninterpreted.
evidence: Twelve radiating spokes are evenly spaced and divide the circle into twelve equal sectors. The concentric rim and hub frame a cyclical, centred structure. The colours alternate in a regular pattern. The figure has no labels, figures or names, so its specific subject cannot be confirmed. The faint writing visible through the parchment is show-through from the verso and does not label the wheel.
